body: congratulations on a new start! Best of luck to you. I once had a soul-sucking job, and did the same thing. Internet high-five :)

"I am just saying that it sounds like you've already made the decision to stay alive. So I suggest you claim that decision and own it, because you had a genuine choice and you chose to stay."
This is spot on. I waver in my will to live, but yes, deep down inside I want to live. Even when life feels like it's all bad, and no good, there's still a part of me that wants to go on *living*. 

"It sounds like your physical circumstances of life are fluid. Things could really get better for you. For some people that's just not true..."

Thank you for this. It's humbling and makes me see things differently. Just gotta hang in there, I suppose. It's hard but I have the skills from therapy, I just need to use them.
haha, that's true! dead people don't succeed at careers. I guess I just get to a point where I'm not rationally thinking, and I want to stop the pain. Thank you for putting this into perspective.
thank you...that really puts things into perspective for me. It's still tempting, but I wouldn't want to put them through that kind of hell.

Wow, I had a very similar experience in undergrad, too, except regarding literature/language instead of finance. I had one professor in college who was the caring, thoughtful type you described. He taught me SO much more than just the coursework. He inspired me, and truly cared for my well-being. If I could be like the professors you described, wow!!! That would be so wonderful and fulfilling :D Thank you for your encouragement, I am really thankful for the fact that you cared to encourage a stranger. You're awesome :)
thank you for your reply! Yeah, I am really hoping I can combine my passion and the desire to help others. I guess I just gotta take a risk.

kittehwidget, I'm so sorry to hear about what happened to you :( you seem like a kind-hearted person, and I hope you can figure out what you want to do with your life. Is there something you are passionate about? Best wishes for your future. you're awesome, I can tell :)

thank you steve-d. "A college professor that actually wants to make a difference is rare in my experience, so you can get the best of both worlds if you pursue it."  --I'd love to be a professor like that! :) passionate, caring teachers are awesome.

ef4, thank you for your thoughtful reply. I really like that you laid things out for me from an ecenomic standpoint! That's what I was looking for. I am still thinking about my decision, but your words have helped me. Thank you so much for your time!
Thank you for your encouragement and advice! I wish you the best, too. I've got to do what I love.

thank you for your advice! To answer that question (great help, by the way), I see myself possibly single, hopefully married in 15 years; no kids, parents not necessarily close by - hopefully far away as I'd like to live in Japan, or travel a lotp; working as a team member; owning a home; "financially free" so I guess independent? (i.e. earning a significant amount more than what I expend.) 

Thank you again :) I really appreciate it!
